title: Compassionate offer decline + reengage playbook
summary: Playbook for handling candidate declines sensitively, preserving employer brand, and actionable re-engagement pathways when circumstances change. Focus: create consistent, empathetic touchpoints and escalation rules to recover high-priority candidates without being intrusive.
background: We observe a ~8% loss rate on offers due to timing, counter-offers, or concerns about role fit. Many are recoverable if we respond with empathy and clear next steps. This doc captures a lightweight, repeatable flow for ACs/recruiters and hiring managers to follow when a candidate declines or asks for time to decide.
objectives: Reduce irreversible offer losses for high-priority candidates by 30% over 6 months
Standardize compassionate decline messages that keep door open for future roles
Provide recruiters and hiring managers with clear decision points and templates
Log candidate reasons and signals for product/compensation feedback loops
out_of_scope: This playbook does not replace formal legal or compensation negotiations for unionized or regulated hires; see Legal for contract amendments.
playbook_steps: Step 0 - Triage: Recruiter marks offer outcome in ATS within 24h and tags reason (compensation, counteroffer, timing, fit, personal)

Step 1 - Compassionate close (0-48h): Send a personalized, human decline acknowledgment (template A) acknowledging their decision, thanking them, and explicitly offering a soft recontact window (e.g., 6 months). Copy the hiring manager on the note for credibility.
Step 2 - Capture signals (0-72h): Quick 3-question call or voice note (optional) to understand primary driver; add short note to candidate record (what we learned and next recommended step).

Step 3 - Internal rubric: If candidate is high-priority (score >=8) then trigger 1:1 hiring manager outreach within 3 business days offering flexibility (start date, part-time ramp, compensation team sync). Otherwise apply standard pipeline tagging and close.

Step 4 - Soft re-engagement calendar: If candidate agreed to stay in touch, create reengagement reminder (90d and 180d) and a brief touch message template (Template B). If declined due to compensation, schedule a market check in 120 days. If declined due to personal reasons, schedule a 6–9 month check-in.

Step 5 - Escalation: If a counteroffer is reported and candidate is critical, open confidential sync with Compensation & Hiring Manager and prepare a counter-proposal within 5 business days (see Escalation notes).
Step 6 - Knowledge loop: Aggregate decline reasons weekly in People Ops review; route compensation signals to Total Rewards and role-fit signals to Hiring Enablement for interview calibration.
decision_points: Is candidate score >=8? If yes, escalate; if no, send standard compassionate close and archive.
Was timing the primary reason? Offer alternative start windows and remote/hybrid options.
Was compensation the primary reason? If role is on a hiring plan bucket that allows flex, open Compensation sync; otherwise flag for future budgeting.
Did candidate request no contact? Respect preference and mark in ATS; do not recontact.
Is there evidence the candidate might be open within 90 days? Use short, non-intrusive recontact cadence.
email_templates:
Template A - Compassionate decline acknowledgment (0-48h)
Subject: Thank you — and we’d love to stay in touch
Hi [Name],
Thank you for letting us know and for the time you spent with the team. I completely understand and respect your decision. If it’s helpful, I’d be happy to stay connected and revisit opportunities down the road — would it be OK to check in in 6 months?
Wishing you the best,
[Recruiter]

Template B - Soft re-engage (90d / 180d)
Subject: Quick hello from Redwood Inference
Hi [Name],
Hope you’ve been well. We had you flagged as someone we’d like to keep in touch with. We’re hiring for roles similar to the one we discussed earlier and I wondered if you’d be open to a short catch-up (15m) in the next few weeks? No pressure — just a quick sync.
Thanks,
[Recruiter]

Template C - Counteroffer escalation note to Hiring Manager + Compensation
Subject: Candidate [Name] declined due to counteroffer — quick sync requested
Hi team,
Candidate [Name] (role: [role]) has declined citing a counteroffer. Candidate score: [score]. Recommend a 20m confidential sync to assess willingness to adjust offer (timing, equity, base).
Link to notes: [ATS link]
Thanks,
[Recruiter]
manager_checklist: Read candidate notes in ATS before any outreach
If candidate is high-priority, reach out personally within 3 business days (short, human note).
Confirm with recruiter whether Compensation will be engaged and what levers are available.
Agree on re-engagement window with candidate (document in ATS).
If recontacting, tailor message to original decline reason (timing vs comp vs fit).
escalation_notes: Do not promise terms on first outreach — get permission to explore options.
Compensation team will only consider adjustments for score >=8 or roles with critical hiring priority.
Keep all compensation discussions confidential and documented in secure HR systems.
logging_and_metrics: Track decline reasons taxonomy weekly (comp, timing, fit, location, other)
Metric: % offers declined where candidate re-engaged within 6 months
Metric: time from decline to re-engagement conversation
Use these signals in monthly people-ops hiring health sync
unresolved_questions: How permissive should managers be on start-date flexibility for critical hires? (need guidance from Exec Recruiting)
What exact score threshold should trigger Compensation escalation in FY26 budget constraints?
Should we automate re-engagement reminders in ATS or manage manually? (ops tradeoff)
Privacy: how long to retain decline reason notes in candidate profile? (legal input needed)
notes_to_self: This is intentionally lightweight — keep recruiter burden low. Pilot with three high-priority roles (infra, applied-ml, product) for Q1 2026 and iterate. Ask ATS team about templated reminders and privacy flags before full rollout.
